rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken Cantonese pattern for an unspecified singular person or thing, with the appropriate classifier replacing 個 when needed.

example.english: I want to buy a popsicle.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 maai5 go3 syut3 gou1

rows.note: Use 一啲 for a small, usually non-count amount or a small degree, such as “a bit” or “a little,” rather than for a countable few items.

example.english: Give me a little time first.
example.jyutping: bei2 ngo5 jat1 di1 si4 gaan3 sin1

rows.note: Use 好多 when “a” occurs in a quantity or degree phrase meaning a lot or a good many.

example.english: I have a lot to do today.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 jau5 hou2 do1 je5 zou6

rows.note: Use 一 before score and quantity units such as hundred, thousand, dozen, or million.

example.jyutping: jat1 baak3 man1 gau3 m4 gau3 aa3
